correctness.rationale: For every n>=3, class classification follows from independence and every occurring neighborhood multiplicity odd: cross-side classes must be one missing-edge pair; single-side classes must be singleton or a whole side if n is even. These independent necessary-and-sufficient classes partition all admissible colorings. Counting disjoint partition families gives the named-palette formula. The binomial/falling-factorial normalization and boundaries q=0 and n odd/even are correct. Standalone direct finite checks passed for 349497 subsets and 1201518 assignments; finite checks are not offered as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: Complete all-palette counting invariant for an infinite standard graph family, establishing the precise difference from square-graph coloring and an unbounded parity oscillation of the minimum number of strong-odd colors. The exact correction is not obtained from known minimum-color or inequality results alone and resolves all color-class types.
